title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON THE PREVENTION OF INSOLVENCY AND STRUCTURAL IMPROVEMENT OF FISHERIES COOPERATIVES
title_original: 수산업협동조합의 부실예방 및 구조개선에 관한 법률 시행령
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON THE PREVENTION OF INSOLVENCY AND STRUCTURAL IMPROVEMENT OF FISHERIES COOPERATIVES

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on the Prevention of Insolvency and Structural Improvement of Fisheries Cooperatives and matters necessary for its enforcement. <Amended on August 19, 2020>

Article 2 (Amounts Excluded from the Scope of Deposits, etc.)
“Amounts received from persons prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the Government and local governments” in the proviso to the part, other than the items, of subparagraph 6 of Article 2 of the Act on the Prevention of Insolvency and Structural Improvement of Fisheries Cooperatives (hereinafter referred to as the “Act”) means amounts received from any of the following persons: <Amended on March 11, 2016; May 10, 2016; August 19, 2020>
1. The Government and local governments;
2. The Bank of Korea established under the Bank of Korea Act, the Financial Supervisory Service established under the Act on the Establishment, etc. of the Financial Services Commission, and the Korea Deposit Insurance Corporation established under the Depositor Protection Act;
3. Insured financial companies under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Depositor Protection Act;
4. Cooperatives.

Article 2-2 (Measures concerning Changes to Prompt Corrective Measures)
“Measures prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as a management diagnosis” in the latter part of the part, other than the subparagraphs, of Article 4-3 of the Act means any of the following measures:
1. A management diagnosis;
2. Suspension or recovery of financial assistance to the relevant cooperative;
3. Other measures that the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries deems necessary for changing prompt corrective measures under Article 4-2 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as “prompt corrective measures”) or consequent upon changes to prompt corrective measures.

Article 3 (Contents of Agreements on the Implementation of Management Normalization)
(1) “Standards for financial soundness prescribed by Presidential Decree” in Article 9 (2) 1 of the Act means the ratio of net capital to total assets prescribed for cooperatives by the Financial Services Commission pursuant to Article 83-3 (1) 1 of the Credit Unions Act. In such cases, loan loss allowances and non-performing loans relating to the calculation of the ratio of net capital to total assets shall include those arising from businesses other than credit business.
(2) “Standards for profitability prescribed by Presidential Decree” in Article 9 (2) 2 of the Act means the following standards:
1. Return on assets or equity;
2. The ratio of expenses to income;
3. Productivity per executive officer or employee.
(3) “Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree” in Article 9 (2) 4 of the Act means matters concerning an increase in equity capital.
(4) Detailed standards concerning the ratio of net capital to total assets under paragraph (1), return on assets or equity, etc. under paragraph (2), an increase in equity capital under paragraph (3), and other such matters shall be prescribed by the Fund Management Committee under Article 21 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Fund Management Committee”).
(5) Deleted. <December 23, 2014>

Article 4 (Non-Disclosure of Agreements)
“Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree” in the proviso to Article 9 (3) of the Act means any of the following matters:
1. Matters concerning the sale of assets held, such as real estate and claims;
2. Matters concerning methods for implementing a management normalization plan.

Article 5 (Opportunity to Provide Explanations concerning Administrative Dispositions)
Where the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries gives an insolvent cooperative an opportunity to provide explanations pursuant to the proviso to Article 10 (2) of the Act, the Minister shall send the relevant insolvent cooperative, no later than 10 days before the date for providing explanations, a notice specifying the details of the disposition, the deadline and method for providing explanations, the procedure to be followed if no explanations are provided, and other matters necessary for providing explanations. <Amended on March 23, 2013>

Article 6 (Determination of Estimated Payment Rates and Estimated Amounts, etc.)
(1) When purchasing claims to deposits, etc. pursuant to Article 13 (1) of the Act, the managing agency under Article 22 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the “managing agency”) shall determine an estimated payment rate by taking into consideration the financial condition of the cooperative and estimating the amount recoverable on claims to deposits, etc. relating to that cooperative if bankruptcy proceedings are conducted.
(2) The estimated value of claims to deposits, etc. that the managing agency is required to pay to depositors, etc. pursuant to Article 13 (2) of the Act shall be the amount calculated by multiplying the value of the claims to deposits, etc. purchased by the managing agency from depositors, etc., as calculated as of the date of the public announcement of payment of insurance benefits (excluding claims to deposits, etc. corresponding to guarantee obligations of depositors, etc. who bear such obligations and the amount of claims to deposits, etc. that are subject to security rights), by the estimated payment rate under paragraph (1).
(3) To pay depositors, etc. the estimated value of claims to deposits, etc. pursuant to Article 13 (2) of the Act, the managing agency shall determine the estimated payment rate under paragraph (1), the period and method for purchasing claims to deposits, etc., and other relevant matters, and obtain a resolution of the Fund Management Committee.
(4) Upon obtaining a resolution under paragraph (3), the managing agency shall give public notice at least once in each of at least two daily newspapers, including one daily newspaper registered under Article 9 (1) of the Act on the Promotion of Newspapers, etc. with the area in which the principal office of the relevant cooperative is located as its principal circulation area, or post the notice on the managing agency's website or by other such means. <Amended on November 24, 2020>

Article 7 (Largest Creditor)
"Largest creditor prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 15 (1) of the Act means the person who, as a result of an investigation of the property status of the relevant cooperative as of any of the following reference dates, holds the largest amount of claims against that cooperative {including claims arising from the payment of insurance benefits, purchase of claims to deposits, etc., financial support, etc. by the Mutual Finance Depositor Protection Fund established and operated pursuant to Article 20 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Fund") after the date of suspension of business, the date of the decision to transfer contracts, the date of the resolution for dissolution, or the date of revocation of authorization for establishment}:
1. A cooperative dissolved due to bankruptcy: The date of suspension of business;
2. A cooperative dissolved due to transfer of contracts: The date of the decision to transfer contracts;
3. A cooperative dissolved for other reasons: The date of the resolution for dissolution or the date of revocation of authorization for establishment.

Article 8 (Requests to Obtain Liability Insurance)
(1) "Cooperatives meeting the criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 17 (1) of the Act means cooperatives that fail to meet the criteria determined by the Fund Management Committee as a result of the assessment of their management status by the president of the National Federation pursuant to Article 142 (2) of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act.
(2) Where the managing agency requests a cooperative to obtain liability insurance pursuant to Article 17 (1) of the Act, it shall make the request in writing, specifically stating the matters determined by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, such as the limit on payment of insurance benefits. <Amended 2013.3.23>
(3) A cooperative requested by the managing agency to obtain liability insurance pursuant to Article 17 (1) of the Act shall obtain liability insurance within 6 months from the date of receipt of the request: Provided, That where unavoidable grounds recognized by the Fund Management Committee exist, such as where obtaining liability insurance is deemed to make normal management of the cooperative difficult, the cooperative shall obtain liability insurance within a period determined by the managing agency not exceeding 2 years.

Article 9 (Methods and Procedures for Investigations)
(1) Where necessary to conduct an investigation under Article 18 (7) of the Act, the managing agency may have its employees investigate books, documents, and other materials concerning the business and property status of corporations in liquidation or bankruptcy estates of insolvent cooperatives and cooperatives at risk of insolvency.
(2) When conducting an investigation pursuant to paragraph (1), the managing agency shall notify the person subject to investigation in advance of necessary matters, such as the grounds for and scope of the investigation: Provided, That this shall not apply where prior notice would make it impossible to achieve the purpose of the investigation due to a risk of destruction of evidence, etc.
(3) When conducting an investigation pursuant to paragraph (1), the managing agency shall give the person subject to investigation sufficient opportunity to state his or her opinions.
(4) Upon completing an investigation, the managing agency shall notify the party concerned of the results of the investigation in writing.

Article 10 (Types of Public Institutions)
"Public institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 19 of the Act means the following institutions:
1. Public institutions under the Act on the Management of Public Institutions;
2. Corporations established pursuant to special Acts;
3. Clearing houses designated pursuant to the Bills of Exchange and Promissory Notes Act or the Check Act.

Article 11 (Operation of the Fund Management Committee)
(1) The chairperson of the Fund Management Committee shall convene and preside over meetings of the Fund Management Committee.
(2) Where the chairperson of the Fund Management Committee is unable to perform the duties of the office due to unavoidable grounds, the vice-chairperson, followed by a person determined by the Fund Management Committee from among its members, shall act on behalf of the chairperson, in that order.
(3) A meeting of the Fund Management Committee shall be convened with the attendance of a majority of all incumbent members, and resolutions shall be passed with the affirmative vote of a majority of the members present.
(4) Where a member of the Fund Management Committee falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the member shall be excluded from the deliberation and resolution of the Fund Management Committee on the relevant agenda item: <Added 2020.8.19>
1. Where the member or the member's spouse or former spouse is a party to the agenda item concerned;
2. Where the member is or was a relative of a party to the agenda item concerned;
3. Where the member has given testimony, made a statement, conducted research, performed services, conducted an appraisal, or provided advice in relation to the agenda item concerned;
4. Where the member belongs to, or has belonged within the most recent 3 years to, a cooperative, enterprise, organization, etc. related to the agenda item concerned.
(5) Where a member falls under any of the grounds for exclusion specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (4) or other circumstances exist that make it difficult to expect impartial deliberation and resolution from the member, a party to the agenda item may challenge that member before the Fund Management Committee, and the Fund Management Committee shall determine by resolution whether to accept the challenge. In such cases, the member against whom the challenge is filed shall not participate in that resolution. <Added 2020.8.19>
(6) Where a member falls under any of the grounds for exclusion specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (4), the member shall recuse himself or herself from the deliberation and resolution of the relevant agenda item. <Added 2020.8.19>
(7) A person who has commissioned or designated a member pursuant to the subparagraphs of Article 21 (2) of the Act may dismiss the member or withdraw the designation if the member fails to recuse himself or herself despite falling under any of the grounds for exclusion specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (4). <Added 2020.8.19>
(8) Matters necessary for the operation of the Fund Management Committee, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (7), shall be determined by the Fund Management Committee. <Amended 2020.8.19>

Article 12 (Issuance of Mutual Finance Depositor Protection Fund Bonds, etc.)
Articles 42 and 43, Article 44 (1), Article 44 (2) 1 through 6, 8, and 9, Articles 45 through 51, Articles 54 through 56, and Articles 58 and 59 of the Enforcement Decree of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the issuance and public subscription, etc. of Mutual Finance Depositor Protection Fund bonds issued by the managing agency for the account of the Fund pursuant to Article 27 (2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "Fund bonds"). In such cases, "National Federation" shall be construed as "managing agency"; "bonds" as "Fund bonds"; "president, representative director in charge of business, or President of Suhyup Bank" as "head of the managing agency"; and "board of directors" as "Fund Management Committee." <Amended 2016.10.25>

Article 13 (Calculation and Payment of Insurance Premiums)
(1) Pursuant to Article 29 (1) of the Act, a cooperative shall pay into the Fund the insurance premiums calculated according to the following formulas within 1 month after the end of each quarter: Provided, That in the case of mutual aid business, payment shall be made within 3 months after the end of each business year. <Amended 2013.3.23>
1. Insurance premiums for credit business = Average balance of deposits and installment savings at the end of each quarter × 1/4 × A rate determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries within a limit of 5/1,000;
2. Insurance premiums for mutual aid business = (Balance of liability reserves at the end of each business year + Total amount of mutual aid premiums received at the end of each business year) × 1/2 × A rate determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries within a limit of 5/1,000.
(2) When calculating insurance premiums for credit business and mutual aid business under paragraph (1), deposits, etc. received from persons specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 shall be excluded.
(3) Where a cooperative fails to pay insurance premiums under paragraph (1) by the due date, it shall pay the premiums into the Fund with a late payment charge added in an amount obtained by multiplying the number of days from the day following the due date for payment of the insurance premiums to the date of payment by an interest rate determined by the Fund Management Committee on the basis of the interest rate applied by the National Federation to mutual finance loans to cooperatives. <Amended 2014.12.23>

Article 13-2 (Reduction of or Exemption from Insurance Premiums)
(1) Pursuant to Article 29-2 (4) of the Act, where the accumulated reserves of the Fund as of the last day of the preceding fiscal year are at or above the lower limit of the target level of the Fund's accumulated reserves set or reset pursuant to Article 29-2 (1) through (3) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "target level" in this Article), the managing agency shall reduce the insurance premiums for the relevant fiscal year following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee.
(2) Pursuant to Article 29-2 (4) of the Act, where the accumulated reserves of the Fund as of the last day of the preceding fiscal year exceed the upper limit of the target level, the managing agency may grant an exemption from insurance premiums for the relevant fiscal year following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee.
(3) Details concerning the procedures and methods for reduction of or exemption from insurance premiums under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be determined by the managing agency following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee.

Article 14 (Calculation of Insurance Benefits)
When calculating insurance benefits payable by the managing agency upon claims by depositors, etc. under Articles 30 (1) and 31 (1) of the Act, the aggregate amount of claims to deposits, etc. shall be the sum of the following amounts:
1. The amount of deposits, etc.;
2. The amount obtained by multiplying the amount under subparagraph 1 by the interest rate determined by the Fund Management Committee, taking into account the average interest rate on deposits, etc. of all cooperatives.

Article 15 (Payment of Advance Payments)
The managing agency may, under Article 30 (2) of the Act, pay depositors, etc. in advance an amount determined by the Fund Management Committee within the insurance benefit payment limit under Article 18 (hereinafter referred to as an "advance payment"): Provided, That where the advance payment exceeds the insurance benefits calculated under Article 31 (1) of the Act, the amount of those insurance benefits shall be the maximum amount payable.

Article 16 (Public Notice of Procedures for Payment of Insurance Benefits, etc.)
Under Article 30 (3) of the Act, the managing agency shall publicly announce the date on which payment of insurance benefits and advance payments will commence, the payment period, the payment methods, and other necessary matters by applying Article 6 (4) mutatis mutandis.

Article 17 (Withholding of Payment of Insurance Benefits)
(1) "Amounts prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 30 (6) of the Act means the following amounts:
1. The amount of claims to deposits, etc. provided by depositors, etc. as collateral to the relevant cooperative for another person;
2. The amount of guarantee obligations owed by depositors, etc. to the relevant cooperative.
(2) Where the managing agency withholds payment of insurance benefits in respect of amounts under paragraph (1) pursuant to Article 30 (6) of the Act, it shall notify the depositors, etc. who claimed payment of those insurance benefits of the following matters in writing, through an information and communications network, by mobile phone text message, or by other such means: <Amended on December 23, 2014>
1. The amount of insurance benefits whose payment is withheld;
2. The grounds for withholding payment of insurance benefits;
3. The period for which payment of insurance benefits is withheld;
4. The procedures and methods for depositors, etc. to claim payment of the withheld insurance benefits where the grounds for withholding payment cease to exist or the withholding period expires.

Article 18 (Limits on Payment of Insurance Benefits)
The limits on payment of insurance benefits under Article 31 (2) of the Act shall be according to the following classifications: <Amended on July 29, 2025>
1. Claims to deposits, etc. falling under Article 2, subparagraph 8 (a) of the Act: 100 million won;
2. Claims to deposits, etc. falling under Article 2, subparagraph 8 (b) of the Act: 100 million won for each of the following categories of claims to deposits, etc.:
(a) Claims to deposits, etc. payable under mutual aid contracts for pension savings accounts under Article 40-2 (1) 1 (c) of the Enforcement Decree of the Income Tax Act (including mutual aid contracts for pension savings accounts under Article 41 of the Addenda to Act No. 11614, the Act Partially Amending the Restriction of Special Taxation Act);
(b) Mutual aid benefits payable upon the occurrence of a ground for payment under a mutual aid contract (excluding mutual aid contracts under item (a)), excluding mutual aid benefits payable upon expiry of the mutual aid coverage period;
(c) Claims to deposits, etc. falling under Article 2, subparagraph 8 (b) of the Act, other than those under items (a) and (b).

Article 19 (Entrustment of Authority)
The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall entrust the following authority to the head of the managing agency under Article 35 of the Act: <Amended on March 23, 2013; August 19, 2020>
1. Designation, management, and revocation of designation of cooperatives subject to management control under Articles 3-3 through 3-5 of the Act;
1-2. Designation of cooperatives at risk of insolvency under Article 4 (2) of the Act;
2. Recommendations or demands for prompt corrective measures under Article 4-2 of the Act with respect to cooperatives at risk of insolvency and their officers.

Article 20 (Processing of Unique Identification Information)
(1) Where unavoidable for the performance of the following duties, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries (including persons entrusted with the authority of the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries under Article 35 of the Act and Article 19 of this Decree) may process data containing resident registration numbers, passport numbers, driver's license numbers, or alien registration numbers under Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act: <Amended on August 19, 2020>
1. Duties concerning designation of insolvent cooperatives or cooperatives at risk of insolvency under Article 4 (2) of the Act;
2. Duties concerning appointment of administrators under Article 4-2 (1) 4 of the Act, the former part of Article 10 (1), paragraph (5) of that Article, and Article 12 (2) of the Act, and requests for registration under Article 12 (5) of the Act;
3. Duties concerning mergers under Article 4-2 (1) 6 of the Act, transfers of business and contracts under subparagraph 7 of that paragraph, and transfers of contracts under Article 10 (2) of the Act;
4. Deleted. <August 19, 2020>
5. Duties concerning requests for the provision of materials or information under Article 19 of the Act;
6. Duties concerning reports and inspections under Article 34 of the Act.
(2) Where unavoidable for the performance of duties concerning inspections under Article 34 (3) of the Act, the Governor of the Financial Supervisory Service established under the Act on the Establishment, etc. of the Financial Services Commission may process data containing resident registration numbers, passport numbers, driver's license numbers, or alien registration numbers under Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act.
(3) Deleted. <August 19, 2020>
(4) Where unavoidable for the performance of the following duties, the managing agency may process data containing resident registration numbers, passport numbers, driver's license numbers, or alien registration numbers under Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act: <Amended on August 19, 2020>
1. Duties concerning requests for designation of insolvent cooperatives or cooperatives at risk of insolvency under Article 4 (1) of the Act;
2. Duties concerning demands for dismissal or suspension from duties of officers of cooperatives and demands for disciplinary action against employees under Article 9-2 (3) of the Act;
3. Duties concerning the presentation of opinions by the Fund Management Committee on appointment of administrators under the former part of Article 10 (1) of the Act;
4. Duties concerning the presentation of opinions by the Fund Management Committee on transfers of contracts under the main clause of the introductory portion of Article 10 (2) of the Act;
5. Duties concerning purchase of claims to deposits, etc. under Article 13 of the Act;
6. Duties concerning appointment of liquidators under Article 15 (1) of the Act and recommendation of bankruptcy trustees under paragraph (2) of that Article;
7. Duties concerning set-off by subrogation under Article 16 of the Act;
8. Duties concerning requests to seek damages under Article 18 (1) of the Act, claims for damages under paragraph (3) of that Article, and intervention in litigation under the former part of paragraph (4) of that Article;
9. Duties concerning collection of insurance premiums under Article 29 (1) of the Act and Article 13 (1) of this Decree;
10. Duties concerning payment of insurance benefits, etc. under Article 30 of the Act;
11. Duties concerning acquisition of the rights of depositors, etc. under Article 33 of the Act.

Article 21 (Criteria for Imposition of Administrative Fines)
The criteria for imposition of administrative fines under Article 39 (1) through (3) of the Act shall be as specified in the attached Table.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 18112, October 30, 2003>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)

Article 2 (Special Cases concerning Limits on Payment of Insurance Benefits)
(1) Where an insured event under subparagraph 9 of Article 2 of the Act occurs during the period from the date on which this Decree enters into force through December 31, 2003, insurance benefits calculated pursuant to Article 31 (1) of the Act shall be paid in full, notwithstanding Article 18, for deposits placed with a cooperative on which no interest is paid (hereinafter referred to as "settlement deposits").
(2) The scope of settlement deposits under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.

Articles 40 through 44 shall each be deleted.
Article 2 of the Addenda to the Decree Amending the Enforcement Decree of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act, Presidential Decree No. 17056, shall be deleted.
